text: UN General Assembly resolutions are not a formal source of international law under Article 38 of the ICJ Statute, and under Articles 10 and 13 of the UN Charter they are recommendations without binding force. They can still carry legal weight as evidence of customary international law when they reflect widespread state practice and *opinio juris*, as the ICJ recognised in *Nicaragua* (1986), and some internal decisions, such as budget decisions under Article 17, are binding within the UN system.
